title: WHO says child restraints are linked to a large drop in infant deaths in crashes
summary: WHO's road-injury fact sheet says the use of child restraints can lead to a 71 percent reduction in deaths among infants.
body: WHO's road-traffic fact sheet, a source outside the US government, says the use of child restraints can lead to a 71 percent reduction in deaths among infants. On the same page, a seat-belt can reduce the risk of death among vehicle occupants by up to half, and correct helmet use cuts motorcyclist deaths by a larger factor. The infant figure is the child-restraint sentence. It is a global fact sheet's statement about restraints, not NHTSA's age rules, and it is not a promise for one journey. The sheet was paraphrased. NHTSA's page is the one that says which direction a US seat should face.
